title: Source-verified engineering memory and shared operating standards
summary: Persistent engineering knowledge capture/retrieval and explicit evidence standards support recurring agent-assisted work across projects.

dates.note: Exact project start/end dates remain unknown. Direct local source/history review on 2026-10-29 supplements the supplied October 5 snapshot and separately dated owner statements. Commit milestones and review dates are not project starts or release dates.

facts.text: Implemented dynamic autonomous creation and retrieval of important engineering memory during running tasks in the coding-agent harness.

Designed knowledge capture that follows conversation history, recognizes superseded decisions, verifies candidate lessons against owning sources and routes durable guidance to authoritative locations while excluding secrets and transient artifacts.
Codified engineering workflows for bootstrap, review, logical-unit commits, GUI debugging and validation, distinguishing collected definitions, execution evidence and passing results.
Standardized read-only Jira and Confluence MCP integration contracts covering OAuth prerequisites, field discovery, pagination, bounded retrieval and export validation.
Current memory behavior does not establish a vector database, distributed memory service, ranking algorithm, consistency model or high-scale operation.

Authored source-aware engineering guidance connecting configuration-engine/RTL topology, interface/resource ownership, GUI lifecycle/renderers, regression selection and release behavior, with authoritative-source routing and explicit stale/generated-document boundaries.

The staged multi-agent workflow specifies planner/analyst/implementer/reviewer responsibilities, evidence handoffs and completion criteria. It is an authored engineering procedure; the shared root orchestrator/agent/evaluation directories remain placeholders rather than an implemented general scheduling engine.

notes: Authored standards are operating procedures; enforcement depends on the selected tool/agent except where executable gates are documented.
Domain guidance does not establish authorship of product algorithms implemented in separate repositories.
